name: AgentOS Functional Iteration
goal: Turn the completed Distribution Alpha from a promotable runtime image path into a more useful AgentOS by adding real functional adapters, operator-facing workflows, long-running control-plane surfaces, and production-distro capability gates without weakening AgentCore or SecurityExecution boundaries.
core_thesis: AgentOS functionality must grow through contracts and adapters, not through a larger agentd binary: runtime_contracts defines typed surfaces, agent_core owns workflow orchestration, security_execution owns side effects, and agentd owns projection and process integration.
non_goals: Do not add normal-mode arbitrary shell execution.
Do not let new adapters bypass SecurityExecutionEngine, PolicyAdapter, CapabilityLease, EffectEnvelope, AuditJournal, rollback, or recovery.
Do not make external LLM, network access, Firecracker, or a host package manager mandatory for baseline acceptance.
Do not collapse runtime_contracts, agent_core, security_execution, and agentd back into a single ownership boundary.
Do not promote a new functional capability without CLI/TUI/operator projection, audit evidence, and a release gate.
Do not treat this workflow as a replacement for production distro hardening; it feeds the production distro path.
primary_acceptance: A functional capability matrix defines user-visible workflows and their required contracts.
Package management, untrusted content, Firecracker execution, update/rollback, and diagnostics/support capabilities are planned as adapter families behind existing runtime boundaries.
Agentd remains a thin composition and projection layer; new capability logic is owned by agent_core, security_execution, runtime_contracts, scripts, or packaging.
Operator-facing commands expose plan preview, approval, denial, audit projection, rollback, and support bundle flows.
Long-running AgentOS control-plane state has health, recovery, migration, and audit retention tasks.
A functional release gate can replay capability workflows in local-only mode and optionally use QEMU at E:\qemu\qemu-system-x86_64.exe.
